title: Quick Open dialog does not display scenes and scripts in the initial file list, but they are searchable
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: Godot v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7657) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900HX (32 threads) - 63.70 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description The Quick Open dialog (Shift+Alt+O on Windows) is designed to quickly locate and open any resource in the project, which should include scenes, scripts, images, audio files, and other Resource files. According to my understanding, its search scope covers all files visible in the FileSystem panel. However, when the Quick Open dialog is first opened (with an empty search field), the displayed file list does NOT include scene (.tscn/.scn) or script (.gd/.cs) files. Despite this, entering any search term will correctly find and display those same scene and script files in the search results. This inconsistency creates a confusing user experience: users expect the initial file list to represent all searchable resource types, but scenes and scripts are missing from the view even though they are technically searchable. Expected behavior: The initial file list of the Quick Open dialog should display all resource types that are within its search scope, including scenes and scripts. Actual behavior: Scenes and scripts are absent from the initial file list but become visible upon searching. This issue appears to be a UI/UX bug in the dialog's initial state rendering, rather than a search functionality issue. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any Godot project that contains at least one scene (.tscn) and one script (.gd) file. 2. Press Shift+Alt+O (Windows) to open the Quick Open dialog. 3. Observe the list of files displayed when the search field is empty. 4. Note that scene and script files are not present in the list. 5. Type any character (e.g., a letter that appears in a scene or script filename) into the search field. 6. Observe that the same scene and script files now appear in the search results. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Any project containing at least one scene and one script file can reproduce this issue. No special setup is required. [my-first-game.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30574194/my-first-game.zip)
